summary: Product analysis feature end-to-end verified. Backend: 5/5 pytest passing for POST /api/products/analyze (text-only INCI via Gemini 2.5 Pro), 400 on empty inputs, 401 unauthenticated, GET /api/products (sorted newest-first, no _id), DELETE /api/products/{id} (200 then 404 on re-delete), input_type='text' persisted, alternatives free of brand names (checked against blacklist La Roche Posay, Sephora, Nivea, CeraVe, etc.), disclaimer present, decision label in {À utiliser|Avec précaution|À éviter}. Frontend: Expo web preview loads, demo login works, 5-tab bottom bar (Accueil, Routines, Produits, Journal, Profil) all rendered. Home screen shows new 'Analyser un produit' card that opens composer in Products tab. Products screen shows header, CTA card, empty state, then history after analysis. Composer has product name input, photo picker, INCI textarea, disclaimer, and 'Analyser ✦' button. End-to-end analysis (INCI sample with Alcohol Denat + Parfum) produced score 25/100 with 'À éviter' red badge, 'Incompatible' verdict, reasons, risks list, and disclaimer at bottom — all displayed correctly.

minor.issue: Both routes are defined TWICE in server.py (lines 582-598 and again at 604-620). FastAPI silently uses the second declaration; functionally identical so tests pass, but this is dead code that should be removed to avoid future drift if one copy is updated.

react_native_issues.issue: Pre-existing console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' from react-native-web. Cosmetic, non-blocking.

action_items: Remove the duplicate route declarations in /app/backend/server.py: delete lines 604-620 (the second copy of @api_router.get('/products') and @api_router.delete('/products/{analysis_id}')). The first definitions on lines 582-598 are the ones that should be kept (or vice versa — either way, dedupe).
Optional: trim file size of products.tsx (470 lines) — close to the 700-line threshold; consider extracting AnalysisViewer and ComposerModal into separate components in /app/frontend/src/components/.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has duplicated /products GET and DELETE handlers — minor code smell, not functional bug.
Product analysis prompt explicitly forbids brand names in alternatives and is enforced by tests (blacklist of 12 known brands). LLM complied on the test sample.
input_type derivation logic is correct: 'photo' (image only), 'text' (INCI only), 'both' (image+text).
Fallback path for unreadable image returns {unreadable: true, message} without persisting — matches PRD requirement (no analysis saved when LLM cannot read).

products.tsx: All interactive elements have testID (new-analysis-btn, quick-scan-card, run-analysis-btn, close-composer-btn, close-viewer-btn, pick-photo-btn, product-name-input, inci-input, history-{id}, delete-{id}, remove-image-btn, unreadable-warn). Excellent test coverage hooks.
Disclaimer 'Analyse indicative, ne remplace pas un avis dermatologique.' is present in BOTH composer and result viewer + persisted in record.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 11 PRD UI checkpoints verified visually + via testID)

seed_data_creation: One product analysis created during test ('UI Test Crème' with input_type=text, score=25, decision=À éviter) — cleaned up via DELETE in pytest. Frontend test left one entry visible in history (named 'UI Test Crème' under demo user); main agent can clear if a fresh demo experience is wanted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://skin-match-7.preview.emergentagent.com. Demo creds demo@skincare.app / Demo1234!. The product analysis LLM call (Gemini 2.5 Pro) takes ~15-25s for text-only input. To test the unreadable fallback, send a tiny non-INCI image with no ingredients_text — it returns {unreadable: true, message: ...} and is NOT persisted. Photo upload via web is non-trivial in Playwright (input[type=file] hidden by expo-image-picker); recommend testing photo path manually or via direct API. Duplicate route in server.py is harmless but should be cleaned up.
rca_of_issue: No bugs. All 11 review items from <features_or_bugs_to_test> verified. The single minor finding is the duplicate FastAPI route definitions which is a copy-paste artifact, not a functional defect.
